title: How to Write a Screenplay With AI in 7 Steps
summary: Learn how to write a screenplay in 7 steps, from logline to rewrite, with the real notes and dialogue of a Flick Residency short and AI help at every step.
body_markdown:
### What is the format of a screenplay?


A screenplay is written in scene headings (INT. or EXT., the place and the time of day), action lines in the present tense, character names in capitals above their dialogue, and short parentheticals for delivery. Pages use 12 point Courier with standard margins, so one page equals about a minute on screen.


### How many pages is a screenplay?


A feature screenplay usually runs 90 to 120 pages, at about one page per minute of screen time. A short film script is 1 to 40 pages, since the Academy counts a film of 40 minutes or less, credits included, as a short.


### How do you start writing a screenplay?


Start with a logline: one sentence that names the main character, what they want and what stands in the way, in under 30 words. Then write a short note for each character and a numbered list of scenes before writing the first page.


### Can AI write a screenplay?


AI can draft scenes, format them and suggest alternatives, but a screenplay worth making needs your idea, your characters' choices and your rewrite. Use AI for variations and read-backs, and write the logline and the final lines yourself.


### What software do you need to write a screenplay?


Any tool that keeps standard format works, from Final Draft to a plain text file in Fountain syntax. Flick's Story view formats a screenplay as you type, imports .fountain, .txt, .fdx, .pdf and .docx files, and downloads a script as PDF or Word.


### What is the difference between a script and a screenplay?


A screenplay is a script written for film, in screenplay format; script is the wider word that also covers plays, TV and video scripts. In everyday use the two words mean the same thing for a film.


### How do you write good dialogue in a screenplay?


Give each character a way of speaking that fits who they are, keep lines short, and let people talk around what they mean. Read every line aloud, or hear it in a generated voice, and cut any line that explains what the audience can already see.
